title: Customer escalation war-room: Nebula Health - 2026-03-15
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for war-room with Nebula Health (customer-facing call at 11:30 PT).
- Capture current impact, suspected root causes, mitigation steps, and clear owner/due dates for follow-ups.

Attendees (internal):
- Jordan Kim (owner, CS escalation lead)
- Sofia Patel (Solutions Eng)
- Marcus Li (SRE on-call)
- Renee Alvarez (Account Exec)
- Ethan Cole (Product PM)

Attendees (customer):
- Priya Menon (Nebula, CTO)
- Daniel Ortiz (SRE)

Background (summary):
- Since ~2026-03-12 22:00 UTC, Nebula Health reports elevated latencies and 5–10% error rate on our hosted inference endpoints (model: redwood-moderate-large-v1).
- Customer traffic spike + long context windows (avg seq len 3.2k) correlated with increased queuing.
- They are on hosted plan, high-throughput. Some requests also getting 502s during autoscaling events.
- Impact: production features degraded for internal customers (affecting clinician workflows). Customer reports potential revenue impact (billing window tomorrow).

Key facts to confirm on the call:
- Exact call pattern: burst windows, peak QPS, typical sequence length distribution (ask Nebula for sample logs).
- Time of first observed errors on their side and any recent config changes (model pin, batch size).
- Whether they use streaming responses or single-shot generation.
- Any recent deployment or rollback on their product side.

Preliminary triage notes (internal):
- Metrics observed (Marcus): increased queue length on auto-scaler groups and sustained GPU saturation on pool-dedicated-host-7 between 2026-03-12 21:45–23:30 UTC.
- Autoscaler observed frequent scale-up/scale-down cycles -> transient 502s during warmups.
- KV cache hit rate for their cookie (customer_id=nebula-123) is low due to high variety in prompts -> less prefix caching benefit.
- Memory pressure reports: model kv cache + large sequence lengths causing memory fragmentation on the runtime.
- Potential suspect: kernel selection fallback for long sequences chooses a slower execution path under current quantization profile.

Immediate mitigation steps (to propose on call):
1) Short term (minutes-2 hours):
   - Temporarily route Nebula traffic to a dedicated hot pool (avoid autoscaler churn). Owner: Jordan (CS) + Marcus (SRE). Due: within 30m.
   - Increase warmup/scale buffer to reduce scale flapping (adjust autoscaler min replicas + cooldown). Owner: Marcus. Due: 45m.
   - Enable aggressive request shedding for non-critical background routes for Nebula (reduce load on inference pool). Owner: Solutions Eng (Sofia). Due: 60m.

2) Medium term (24–72 hours):
   - Run a profiling job on Nebula's representative prompts to verify kernel selection and memory usage. Owner: Ethan (Product) + Marcus. Due: 48h.
   - Propose a temporary model variant with shorter context window (or prompt pre-processing) to reduce KV pressure. Owner: Sofia + Jordan. Due: 48h.
   - Work with Nebula to add lightweight caching for repeated prefixes (engineering playbook). Owner: Jordan -> coordinate with customer devs. Due: 72h.

3) Postmortem/long term:
   - Update autoscaler heuristics for rapid bursty traffic (learned from this incident). Owner: Platform Eng (TBD). Due: next sprint.
   - Add dashboard for per-customer KV cache hit/miss and memory fragmentation signals. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2 weeks.

Data/ask from customer during call:
- Share last 2 hours of client-side request IDs and timestamps (for tracing).
- Representative prompt set (5–10 examples) to run internal repro.
- Consent for us to route a small percentage of traffic to a dedicated hot pool for 30–60 minutes for mitigation.

Communication plan:
- 11:30 PT: customer call (we will present mitigation plan + immediate steps).
- Post-call: 30-min sync to confirm actions and update Confluence.
- Status updates every 2 hours in #cs-esc-nebula Slack thread.
- If mitigation reduces errors to <1% for 30 minutes, schedule a follow-up in 24 hours to close.

Runbook snippets to reference on call:
- Autoscaler warmup config (link in Confluence).
- Routing playbook: how to pin traffic to hot pool and rollback.
- Kernel fallback debug steps and profiling commands (Marcus has snippet).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Can we commit to a dedicated hot pool briefly for a hosted customer without an SLA change? (Legal/ops implication) -> Renee to confirm with sales/support policy.
- Is there appetite to accept a temporary model variant by Nebula product team? (potential quality regression) -> discuss on call.

Notes for call script (Jordan):
- Quick apology + ownership, explain what we know, propose immediate mitigations, ask for permission to route to hot pool and to get prompt examples.
- Avoid deep technical jargon; commit to timeline and follow-ups.

Action items (captured):
- Jordan: Kick off customer call + request prompt examples + confirm consent for hot pool routing. Due: 11:35 PT (on call).
- Marcus: Prepare hot-pool routing playbook + execute routing if customer ok. Due: 11:50 PT.
- Sofia: Prepare profiling flow and temporary model-variant proposal. Due: 2026-03-16 17:00 UTC.
- Renee: Check entitlements/legal for temporary hot-pool routing and inform customer about potential billing/credits. Due: 2026-03-15 EOD PT.
- Ethan: Start codelab to repro memory fragmentation with provided prompts. Due: 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC.
- All: Post updates to Confluence page and #cs-esc-nebula Slack thread after call. Due: immediate after call.

Follow-up meeting:
- Schedule 90-min technical sync with Nebula SREs + our SREs (include product) tomorrow 09:00 PT if mitigation incomplete.

Scratch notes / quick logs:
- Marcus: saw p95 latency spike to 2.8s (baseline 0.6s) at 2026-03-12 22:12 UTC.
- Error traces show 502s with backend task timeout during scale events.
- Recent infra change? autoscaler cooldown param touched on 2026-03-10 by infra team (MR 412).

End-state for closure:
- Nebula errors <1% for 4 consecutive hours + sign-off from Priya that clinician flows restored.
- Postmortem published with root cause and remediation items.

Misc / notes to self:
- Keep messages concise; customers get nervous with too many technical unknowns.
- If hot-pool route fails, fall back to throttling non-critical routes and offer credits.
- Make sure billing notice is prepped in case traffic routing increases short-term cost.

-- Jordan
